question: What will be the percentage change in front-month Henry Hub natural gas futures (NG=F on Yahoo Finance) from the close on 2026-08-12 to the close on 2026-09-17?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to 100 x (close on 2026-09-17 / close on 2026-08-12 - 1), using daily closes of NG=F on Yahoo Finance. If there is no close on 2026-09-17, the last close before it is used.
baseline:
Computed by code from Yahoo Finance daily closes for NG=F: latest close 2.8040 on 2026-08-12.
Target date 2026-09-17 is 25 trading observations ahead. Percentiles of the price on the target date,
from the empirical distribution of 25-observation returns over the last 3 years (last year weighted double):
p5: 1.9783, p10: 2.1673, p25: 2.4717, p50: 2.7774, p75: 3.1707, p90: 3.637, p95: 3.9943
This ignores news and known events; adjust for them. Check the symbol matches the resolution source
(exchange, contract month, close vs settlement price).
research:
I couldn't confirm the August 12 close on Yahoo itself, because the proxy blocked every page fetch. The best figure I found is about $2.804/MMBtu for the September contract (NGU26), taken from search snippets only. The front month also switches from the September to the October contract before September 17, so the resolution compares two different contracts.

## 1. Resolution source
- Resolution uses Yahoo Finance NG=F daily closes. The Yahoo history page would not load, so I could not read the official value.
- 2026-08-12: Snippets say September Nymex gas settled at **2.804** on Wednesday, up from Tuesday. They credit a hotter short-term weather forecast. [Premier Energy, Aug 12](https://www.premierenergymanagement.com/post/natural-gas-marketwatch-august-12-2026-mid-week-cooling-and-strategic-outlook)
- 2026-08-11: The September contract closed at **$2.767**. [Sprague Energy](https://www.spragueenergy.com/september-nymex-natural-gas-futures-contract-closed-at-2-767-on-tuesday-august-11th/)
- **The contract switch:** the September contract expires 2026-08-27, so on 2026-09-17 NG=F will be the October contract (NGV26). I could not find the October-minus-September price gap as of August 12. If October trades above September, the switch alone adds to the measured change. [Brief](https://www.thebrief.news/en/standard/article/6575/august-natural-gas-futures-expire-today-a-1772-monthly-slide-and-a-winter-curve-that-disagrees)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the question. The resolution date is about 25 trading days after August 12.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-12: Prices rose about 1.3% on hotter near-term forecasts. Analysts expected a roughly 33 Bcf storage build for the week ending Aug 7. [Premier Energy](https://www.premierenergymanagement.com/post/natural-gas-marketwatch-august-12-2026-mid-week-cooling-and-strategic-outlook)
- 2026-08-10 (week of): Futures were "pinned near a 14-week low". [Energy Intelligence](https://www.energyintel.com/0000019f-ec59-dc58-addf-ed5da1dd0003)
- 2026-08-07: AGA said Henry Hub spot and futures had stayed below $3 through August despite warmer-than-normal weather. Its latest futures settle was **$2.60** on Aug 5. [AGA](https://www.aga.org/research-policy/resource-library/natural-gas-market-indicators-august-7-2026/)
- 2026-08-06: The September contract hit a one-month low of 2.616. Futures fell to multi-month lows after a large storage build. [Barchart NGU26](https://www.barchart.com/futures/quotes/NGU26), [CME video](https://www.cmegroup.com/videos/2026/08/06/natural-gas-futures-fell-to-multi-month-lows-on-storage-build-8.html)
- 2026-08-04: The September contract closed at $2.682 as cooling demand faded. [Sprague](https://www.spragueenergy.com/september-nymex-natural-gas-futures-contract-closed-at-2-682-on-tuesday-august-4th/)
- 2026-08 (EIA August outlook): EIA cut its Q3 2026 Henry Hub forecast to **$2.87**, 50 cents below its July forecast. It cited weaker LNG feedgas demand and strong production. It expects storage of 3,985 Bcf in October, the most heading into winter since 2016. [EIA STEO Aug 2026](https://eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/aug26.pdf), [PGJ](https://pgjonline.com/news/2026/august/us-eia-expects-highest-natural-gas-inventories-in-a-decade-heading-into-winter)
- 2026-07-28: The August contract expired at $2.662 after a 17.72% monthly drop. Winter contracts were priced well above the front month. [Brief](https://www.thebrief.news/en/standard/article/6575/august-natural-gas-futures-expire-today-a-1772-monthly-slide-and-a-winter-curve-that-disagrees)

## 4. Base rates
- **Typical size of moves:** front-month gas usually swings about 45-65% a year in annualized terms. Over about 25 trading days that works out to roughly ±13-20% for one standard deviation, and moves of ±25% or more happen. This is my own calculation, not a sourced figure.
- **Past years, mid-August to mid-September:** from memory, these moves were mostly moderate, in the single digits to low teens of percent. For example, 2024 went from about $2.2 to about $2.35 (gain), and 2023 from about $2.8 to about $2.65 (loss). I could not check these figures against a source in this session.
- **Price level:** prices are near multi-month lows, with storage about 195 Bcf above the five-year average as of the week ending July 31. That figure came from a search summary and I did not check it against EIA. [FXEmpire](https://www.fxempire.com/forecasts/article/natural-gas-news-eia-report-could-extend-selloff-as-storage-surplus-pressures-futures-1615240)

## 5. Other forecasts
- EIA's August outlook forecasts a Q3 2026 Henry Hub spot average of $2.87, close to the current futures price. [EIA](https://eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/aug26.pdf)
- I found Kalshi natural gas price markets for September dates, but could not get prices dated on or before August 13, so I report none. I found no Polymarket or Manifold market.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **EIA weekly storage reports**, Thursdays at 10:30 ET: Aug 13, 20 and 27, and Sep 3, 10 and 17. The Sep 17 report comes out on the resolution day. [Investing.com calendar](https://www.investing.com/economic-calendar/natural-gas-storage-386)
- **2026-08-27:** the September contract expires and NG=F switches to October. [Brief](https://www.thebrief.news/en/standard/article/6575/august-natural-gas-futures-expire-today-a-1772-monthly-slide-and-a-winter-curve-that-disagrees)
- **Around early-to-mid September:** the next EIA outlook comes out (exact date not checked). [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/pressroom/releases/press591.php)
- **Other drivers:**
  - Late-summer heat or cooling, including the heat dome over the South.
  - The peak of Atlantic hurricane season. Gulf storms can cut LNG demand, which is bearish, or cut production, which is bullish.
  - LNG feedgas levels and new export capacity.
  - Record production levels.
